verdicts.quote: A waiting member receives a confirmed booking when they become next for an available seat. No claim or response is required.

the member whose join was accepted first gets it. ... the operator sees a definite order that is retained for later allocation. ... Operators can inspect order but cannot use the waitlist to move an entry ahead of another.

The member gets the same cancellation effects as for an equivalent ordinary booking, including any applicable refunds, charges, and entitlement restoration. Existing rules and amounts are unconfirmed.
verdicts.missing: Whether an auto-promoted member who does not attend (no-show) or cancels late is penalized under the existing no-show/late-cancellation policy is not stated explicitly.

verdicts.quote: After the waiting member closes the app, an eligible release can still result in a confirmed booking. The runtime's background execution rules, scheduling cadence and execution deadline are unconfirmed.
verdicts.missing: Triggers (cancellation, capacity increase, hold release) are named, but the background cadence and how quickly processing must happen are left undecided.

verdicts.quote: If an equivalent ordinary confirmation would send a booking message, a promotion triggers the same confirmation policy. Existing channels, recipients, contents, and delivery rules are unconfirmed.
verdicts.missing: The channel and message content are deferred to an unconfirmed existing policy, and nothing says what happens when sending fails (in-app status under C-59 is the only fallback stated).

verdicts.quote: With several eligible people waiting and one available seat, at most one receives a booking from that release. ... confirmed seats plus any existing holds ... do not exceed current capacity because of that promotion.
If an ordinary booking and a promotion for the same member race, no second live confirmed booking is added for the member on that occurrence.
A promoted booking has the same payment treatment as an equivalent ordinary booking ... Applicable charges, credits, amounts, currency, and payment timing are unconfirmed.
verdicts.missing: When payment is taken is unconfirmed, and what happens to the entry when a payment attempt fails (ends vs. stays waiting vs. retry) is not specifically decided.

verdicts.quote: An eligible join is accepted even with many members already waiting, subject to service availability. There is no configured maximum number of waiting members per occurrence.

When ordinary booking closes, every still-waiting entry for the occurrence ends with booking closed as the reason. ... If ordinary booking closes before an allocation takes effect, the requester cannot receive a booking from that allocation.
Increasing capacity above occupied seats while booking remains open lets an eligible waiting member receive a booking. ... A confirmed member retains their booking after capacity is reduced
When the occurrence is canceled, every still-waiting entry ends with occurrence canceled as the reason.
their status as waiting, booked through the waitlist, withdrawn, or ended without booking ... a definite order that is retained for later allocation.
verdicts.missing: The entry's states and an acceptance order are defined, but no record with a join timestamp is specified and whether position is stored or derived is not decided.

verdicts.quote: a completed outcome can still be inspected. Exact retention duration is unconfirmed and follows the existing occurrence record lifecycle.
verdicts.missing: How long entries are kept after the class has run, and whether they are purged, is left unconfirmed.

verdicts.quote: A member cannot see other entries, identities, order, or outcomes through member-facing views or requests. ... A member can tell whether their entry is waiting from its status alone.
verdicts.missing: Hiding other people's identities is covered, but whether the member is shown their own position is not decided.

verdicts.quote: The occurrence's waitlist view can show withdrawn, booked through the waitlist, and ended without booking ... Operators cannot force a promotion through the waitlist view.
verdicts.missing: Viewing and the absence of manual promote/remove are covered, but whether staff can see when each promotion happened (a timestamp) is not stated.

verdicts.quote: An authorized operator can pause new waitlist joins across all occurrences with one control. ... can open intake for all eligible occurrences with one control.
The runtime's background execution rules, scheduling cadence and execution deadline are unconfirmed. No fixed waitlist-specific turnaround time is promised for this background work.
verdicts.missing: No latency bound is set; the builder still has to decide how promptly promotion runs after a cancellation.

verdicts.quote: A member can confirm a seat through the existing booking flow when there is capacity available for direct booking ... previously confirmed seats still appear in the member's bookings with the same active status
After enablement, an otherwise eligible full occurrence created before rollout can accept a join. ... is not added to a waitlist by deployment.
